exposure: Continuity of care (CoC) with a midwife
Continuity of care (CoC) with a doctor
outcome: Feeling in control of decision making
Perceived positive support from health care provider for VBAC
Likelihood of being active in labour
Perception of VBAC as less traumatic than previous caesarean
cohort: The study included 490 women from every State and Territory in Australia who had planned a Vaginal Birth After Caesarean (VBAC) in the past 5 years.
finding: Women planning a VBAC benefited from Continuity of Care models, particularly midwifery continuity of care, leading to increased feelings of control, support, autonomy, and respect during their planning process.
mod_finding: Women found having a VBAC less traumatic than their previous caesarean.
cross-section timing: Past 5 years prior to the survey
